column18: Sparse training recipe (ghost neurons, skip connections, init, labels) improves lottery ticket, SNIP, GRASP, SynFlow and random masks
Random buildup then LTH-like elimination with binary search; over 98% pruned matching full-network performance on three image datasets
IMP viewed as renormalization group flow; ResNet-50 and BERT transferable winning tickets show common flow properties; no efficiency figures
Fourier analysis of magnitude pruning plus two-stage prune and frequency-domain distillation retraining; CIFAR-10/100; no efficiency figures
LTH-style hierarchical structured pruning of prompt tokens closes gap with fine-tuning on SuperGLUE at smaller model scales
Hybrid ANN/SNN/BNN processor: 0.99 to 4.38 uJ/class across EEG, ECG, EMG and spike tasks; no ANN-SNN comparison on same task
Dendrite-inspired CNN on FPGA: 10.7 uJ/frame, 88% CIFAR-10; 94.4x better energy efficiency, 6% higher accuracy than spiking CNN FPGA
SNN accelerator 65nm synthesis: DVS-Gesture 92.7% accuracy, 24.3 uJ/image; MNIST 349.6 KFPS, 0.52 uJ/image; sparsity-exploiting dataflow
Fabricated 65nm mixed-signal ESN spiking processor: 95.35% MNIST accuracy, 12.92 nJ per classification; sparse connections optimized
Hybrid RRAM CNN and SRAM SNN tracking SoC, 73.53 TOPS/W in title; abstract gives no ANN-SNN comparison results
SCNN on Loihi simulator: 6.2 uJ, 9.5 ms, sensitivity 92.2, specificity 97.3; CNN on MCU 93.4 and 99.1
Title: 22nm 0.43 pJ/SOP sparsity-aware hybrid SNN/ANN in-memory system; abstract is background only, no results
Single-shot layer-wise channel pruning under computational constraints; reduces memory, speeds up, raises throughput, no figures
Proves equivariant strong LTH for G-equivariant networks with optimal overparametrization; verified by pruning E(2)-steerable CNNs and GNNs
DNN vs SNN under BFV encryption on FashionMNIST: SNN up to 40% higher accuracy at low modulus, longer execution time
Learnable spike coding for spiking RL: latency down to 0.8% of other SRL methods, energy efficiency up to 5X DNNs

ANN-SNN conversion with clipping layer and potential initialization: MNIST 96.18% at 2 time steps, 97.68% at 16; only time-steps

Converted spiking ResNet beats SRCNN and unconverted ResNet at low channel SNR; 68% lower storage and energy requirements

Federated proactive caching using lottery hypothesis for privacy; beats Thompson Sampling in caching efficiency; no model-efficiency figures

LIF SNN circuit fault simulation: 85.25% neuron loss tolerated in second layer, 93.33% fault tolerance; pruning reduces connections
Shallow converted-ResNet SNN on few neuromorphic devices: accuracy over 80%, about 1/130 the energy of GPU running same DNN
